TASKBAR TIMER  v1.0
===================

A countdown timer that sits on your taskbar showing the time remaining as
readable text, right next to the clock. Left-click to start, right-click for
options. It alerts you by flashing, by sound, or both.

Works on Windows 10 and Windows 11.


HOW TO INSTALL
--------------

1. Copy this whole folder onto the computer (Desktop is fine). Keep the files
   together - the installer needs them side by side.

2. Double-click  Install.cmd

3. Windows may show a blue box saying "Windows protected your PC". This is
   normal and is explained below. Click "More info", then "Run anyway".

4. Answer the one question it asks - whether you want the timer to start
   automatically with Windows.

That's it. The timer appears on your taskbar showing 30:00 in amber.


ABOUT THE "WINDOWS PROTECTED YOUR PC" WARNING
---------------------------------------------

You will probably see this, and it is worth understanding rather than just
clicking through.

Windows shows that warning for any program that has not been through a paid
commercial code-signing process. It is not a virus warning and it does not mean
anything was detected. It means only that Microsoft has not seen this exact file
signed by a registered company. Small tools written for personal use are almost
never signed, because the certificates cost hundreds of pounds a year.

Click "More info", then "Run anyway".

Your antivirus may also scan the file the first time it runs. That is fine, and
it should only happen once.


HOW TO USE IT
-------------

  Left-click                 Start or pause the countdown
  Left-click while alarming  Silence the alarm
  Left-drag                  Move it somewhere else on screen
  Right-click                Everything else

The right-click menu gives you:

  5 to 90 minutes    Preset lengths - picking one starts it straight away
  Custom...          Any length. Understands 25, 45m, 1h30m, 90s, 2:30
                     A plain number means minutes.
  Start / Pause
  Reset

  Alert with         Flash, Sound, or Both
  Volume             10% to 100%. Picking a level plays the alarm so you can
                     hear what you are choosing.
  Alert for          How long the alarm keeps going: until you stop it, or
                     15 seconds up to 5 minutes

  Snap back to the tray   Returns it next to the clock after you have dragged it
  Start with Windows      Tick or untick - it remembers
  Exit


WHAT THE COLOURS MEAN
---------------------

  Amber digits    Paused, or not started yet
  Green digits    Counting down
  Red digits      Last tenth of the time you set, so the warning comes
                  proportionally - 3 minutes into a 30 minute countdown,
                  30 seconds into a 5 minute one
  Flashing red    Time is up


WHAT THE INSTALLER CHANGES
--------------------------

  - Copies one file, TaskbarTimer.exe, to C:\Tools\TaskbarTimer
    (or to your AppData folder if it cannot write to C:\Tools)
  - Adds a Start Menu shortcut under your own user account
  - Adds one startup entry, but only if you answer yes when asked
  - Starts the timer

It does not change system settings, does not need administrator rights, does not
touch anything belonging to other users of the PC, and does not connect to the
internet. Ever.


SETTINGS
--------

Most things are on the right-click menu. A few extras live in a file called
settings.ini, which appears next to the program after first use:

  FontSize             Size of the digits, default 11
  Bold                 true or false
  FlashTickMs          How fast the alarm flashes, default 250
  SoundFile            Full path to your own .wav file for the alarm.
                       Leave blank to use the built-in tone.

Close the timer before editing that file by hand, or your changes will be
overwritten when it next saves.


TO REMOVE IT
------------

Double-click  Uninstall.cmd  in this folder.

It stops the timer, removes the startup entry, deletes the Start Menu shortcut
and deletes the installed folder. Nothing is left behind.


REQUIREMENTS
------------

Windows 10 or Windows 11, and Microsoft .NET Framework 4.x - which is already
part of both. The installer checks and will tell you if it is somehow missing.
